class.name: TireData
class.brief_description: A resource that defines tire parameters for the tanh-based tire model.
class.description: TireData is a [Resource] that configures tire behavior: grip (friction coefficient), radius, brake power, bearing drag, peak slip angle (controls how sharp the tire bites), relaxation times for force smoothing, combined-grip exponent, and self-aligning torque trail parameters. [Wheel] computes the internal SAT moment as [code]lateral_force * trail[/code]; because its applied world lateral force is [code]-right_tangent * lateral_force[/code], SAT opposes that applied force. Tire parameters are copied to each [Wheel] during running-gear setup.

members.member: Longitudinal (forward) tire friction coefficient. Higher values increase grip for acceleration and braking.
Lateral (cornering) tire friction coefficient. Higher values increase grip when turning.
Optional [Curve] resource for custom longitudinal friction response. Maps normalized slip velocity (0-2) to a friction multiplier. Overrides the default tanh-based model.
Optional [Curve] resource for custom lateral friction response. Maps normalized slip angle (0-2) to a friction multiplier. Overrides the default tanh-based model.

Exponent [code]p[/code] for combining normalized longitudinal and lateral force. The value is clamped to [1, 16] (default 2). [code]p=2[/code] is the established friction ellipse; larger values progressively retain more simultaneous normalized longitudinal/lateral force before limiting. The configured value is copied to each [Wheel] during setup.

Pneumatic trail contribution to simplified self-aligning torque, in metres. Its influence rolls off quadratically with normalized absolute slip angle. Default: 0.02 m. This is a model parameter, not a physical caster-geometry calculation.
Mechanical trail contribution to simplified self-aligning torque, in metres. Default: 0.02 m.
Maximum brake torque in Newton-meters at full brake input.
Wheel bearing and rotational drag coefficient. Higher values slow wheel spin faster.
Slip angle in degrees at which lateral force reaches ~76% of its maximum. Lower values (e.g. 6-8) give sharper tire bite; higher values (12-16) give softer, more progressive response.
Force relaxation time in seconds at zero speed. Lower values make the tire respond faster when stationary or slow (42 ms default).
Force relaxation time in seconds at high speed (30 m/s+). Lower values give instant force response (10 ms default).
Width of the tire tread in metres. Used by [TireSkid] to set the ribbon width of skid marks.
